rows.translation: 外貌
rows.raw: "Appearance"

rows.original: Take a gander at Busky.
rows.translation: 仔细端详巴斯基。
rows.raw: "Take a gander at Busky."

rows.original: Talk
rows.translation: 交谈
rows.raw: "Talk"

rows.original: “Sure, I’m down to talk, whaddya wanna know?” Busky asks as he fold his arms and leans back against the wall, a calm, placid expression painted on his face, as if he has nothing to hide.
rows.translation: “当然，我愿意聊聊。你想知道什么？”巴斯基抱起双臂靠在墙上问道，脸上神情平静而放松，仿佛没有任何事情需要隐瞒。
rows.raw: "“Sure, I’m down to talk, whaddya wanna know?” Busky asks as he fold his arms and leans back against the wall, a calm, placid expression painted on his face, as if he has nothing to hide."

rows.original: “Name’s Buskurt Agnos, people just call me Busky though, and honestly I’m just your run of the mill New Texan Bull.” Busky says casually. “Not much different than Ol’ Big T. himself.”
rows.translation: “我叫巴斯克特·阿格诺斯，不过大家都叫我巴斯基。老实说，我只是个普通得不能再普通的新德克萨斯公牛。”巴斯基随意地说道。“和老大T本人没什么区别。”
rows.raw: "“Name’s Buskurt Agnos, people just call me Busky though, and honestly I’m just your run of the mill New Texan Bull.” Busky says casually. “Not much different than Ol’ Big T. himself.”"

rows.original: “So you spend every waking moment ogling at the biggest pair of breasts in the room,” you joke. Busky himself chuckles for a second before responding.
rows.translation: “所以你醒着的每一刻都在盯着房间里最大的那对乳房看，”你开玩笑道。巴斯基本人也轻笑片刻，随后回答。
rows.raw: "\n\n“So you spend every waking moment ogling at the biggest pair of breasts in the room,” you joke. Busky himself chuckles for a second before responding."

rows.original: “Not exactly a woman person myself, if you know what I mean. Instead of Aphrodite, I’d rather get with Priapus, or as he’s known around here, ‘Brynn’, heh. Here’s a tip, with him, there’s no such thing as ‘just the tip’, made that mistake myself and by the end of it, I couldn’t sit down for a month.”
rows.translation: “其实我对女人没什么兴趣，你懂我的意思。比起阿芙洛狄忒，我更想和普里阿普斯上床，或者照本地叫法，‘布莱恩’，嘿嘿。给你个忠告，和他做的时候可不存在‘只进去一点’这种事。我自己就犯过这个错，结果整整一个月都坐不下来。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Not exactly a woman person myself, if you know what I mean. Instead of Aphrodite, I’d rather get with Priapus, or as he’s known around here, ‘Brynn’, heh. Here’s a tip, with him, there’s no such thing as ‘just the tip’, made that mistake myself and by the end of it, I couldn’t sit down for a month.”"

rows.original: You chuckle, amused at Busky’s honesty. It seems like everyone really has nothing to hide in New Texas.
rows.translation: 你被巴斯基的坦率逗笑了。看来新德克萨斯真的人人都毫不遮掩。
rows.raw: "\n\nYou chuckle, amused at Busky’s honesty. It seems like everyone really has nothing to hide in New Texas."

rows.original: “Anyway,” Busky starts, “who are you exactly? Haven’t seen your face ‘round here.”
rows.translation: “总之，”巴斯基开口道，“你到底是谁？以前没在这里见过你。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Anyway,” Busky starts, “who are you exactly? Haven’t seen your face ‘round here.”"

rows.original: You introduce yourself as Steele, [pc.name] Steele.
rows.translation: 你自我介绍说自己叫斯蒂尔，[pc.name]·斯蒂尔。
rows.raw: "\n\nYou introduce yourself as Steele, [pc.name] Steele."

rows.original: “Kind of an odd last name; it Terran or something?”
rows.translation: “这个姓有点特别；是地球人的姓还是什么？”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Kind of an odd last name; it Terran or something?”"

rows.original: You awkwardly explain Steele Co. and how you’re the soon to be CEO while Busky nods in understanding.
rows.translation: 你尴尬地解释了斯蒂尔公司，以及自己即将成为首席执行官的事，巴斯基则理解地点点头。
rows.raw: "\n\nYou awkwardly explain Steele Co. and how you’re the soon to be CEO while Busky nods in understanding."

rows.original: “Cool. Never really paid attention to Steele Co. myself, not much of a big deal to me since I don’t really have much need for tetratazmanian carbonoid alloys or whatever. Anyway, nice to meet you, [pc.name].”
rows.translation: “挺酷的。我自己从来没怎么关注斯蒂尔公司，毕竟我用不着什么四塔兹马尼亚碳化合金之类的东西，对我来说没什么大不了。总之，很高兴认识你，[pc.name]。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Cool. Never really paid attention to Steele Co. myself, not much of a big deal to me since I don’t really have much need for tetratazmanian carbonoid alloys or whatever. Anyway, nice to meet you, [pc.name].”"

rows.original: “Take a look ‘round here. Ya see any other shops selling stuff for guys? I mean, aside from Ellie selling Suma, there’s nothing, which is why I set up shop here, went through a couple of names before finally settling on Straps. It cost a crap ton to construct and stock, so I took out a loan from Ol’ T. He’s pretty reasonable, no interest or anything. All I’ve gotta do is give him a bit of control on our stock till I pay him back.” Busky pauses and glances at the mods lining the wall behind the counter. “‘Cept for some reason he doesn’t want me selling Treatment Medipens. Plus he tends to let me order shipments first, and then blacklist stuff after the fact. Got a whole store of products collecting dust in the back.”
rows.translation: “看看周围。你在这里看到任何其他专卖男人用品的店了吗？我的意思是，除了艾莉卖的苏玛以外什么都没有。所以我才在这里开店，换了好几个名字后才最终定下‘束带’。建店和进货花了海量信用点，所以我向老T借了笔钱。他很通情达理，没收利息。还清之前，我只需要让他对店里的存货有一点决定权。”巴斯基停下来，看了眼柜台后面墙上的身体模组。“只是，不知为什么他不让我卖改造剂注射器。而且，他经常先让我下单，等货都订了才把东西列入黑名单。现在后面有整整一店的产品都在吃灰。”
rows.raw: "“Take a look ‘round here. Ya see any other shops selling stuff for guys? I mean, aside from Ellie selling Suma, there’s nothing, which is why I set up shop here, went through a couple of names before finally settling on Straps. It cost a crap ton to construct and stock, so I took out a loan from Ol’ T. He’s pretty reasonable, no interest or anything. All I’ve gotta do is give him a bit of control on our stock till I pay him back.” Busky pauses and glances at the mods lining the wall behind the counter. “‘Cept for some reason he doesn’t want me selling Treatment Medipens. Plus he tends to let me order shipments first, and then blacklist stuff after the fact. Got a whole store of products collecting dust in the back.”"

rows.original: You ask about what kind of products are back there.
rows.translation: 你问后面都放着什么样的产品。
rows.raw: "\n\nYou ask about what kind of products are back there."

rows.original: “Ever see a bull with milky pecs?” he chuckles.
rows.translation: “见过胸肌能产奶的公牛吗？”他笑着问道。
rows.raw: "\n\n“Ever see a bull with milky pecs?” he chuckles."

rows.original: You can’t say that you have.
rows.translation: 你确实没见过。
rows.raw: "\n\nYou can’t say that you have."

rows.original: “Anyway, I was a real bookworm before I took The Treatment, studied a bit of everything, took a bunch of business classes and so here I am. Not doing too bad if I say so myself. Thankfully the Treatment didn’t mess with me too much, can still focus on work, though, if there’s a particularly large butt passing by...” he trails off for a moment, before before snapping back to reality, “‘course, if it doesn’t work out I could always become a breeding stud to pay T. back. Anyway I finalized the location, constructing right next to the gym, seein’ how I spend most of my free time there anyway. Plus it’s a good way to get people to notice the place.”
rows.translation: “总之，我接受改造疗程前可是个十足的书呆子，什么都学过一点，还上过一大堆商业课程，所以现在才会在这里。要我自己说，经营得还算不错。幸好改造疗程没有太大影响我，工作时还是能集中注意力，不过，要是有个特别大的屁股从旁边经过...”他一时走了神，然后才猛然回过神来，“当然，要是经营不下去，我也随时可以当配种公牛还老T的钱。总之，我最终定下这个店址，建在健身房旁边，毕竟我大部分空闲时间本来就在那里。这也是吸引别人注意这家店的好办法。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Anyway, I was a real bookworm before I took The Treatment, studied a bit of everything, took a bunch of business classes and so here I am. Not doing too bad if I say so myself. Thankfully the Treatment didn’t mess with me too much, can still focus on work, though, if there’s a particularly large butt passing by...” he trails off for a moment, before before snapping back to reality, “‘course, if it doesn’t work out I could always become a breeding stud to pay T. back. Anyway I finalized the location, constructing right next to the gym, seein’ how I spend most of my free time there anyway. Plus it’s a good way to get people to notice the place.”"

rows.original: You ask about The Treatment and what his life was like before he took it.
rows.translation: 你询问改造疗程，以及他接受疗程前过着怎样的生活。
rows.raw: "You ask about The Treatment and what his life was like before he took it."

rows.original: <i>“I knew you’d ask about that sooner or later.
rows.translation: <i>“我就知道你迟早会问这个。
rows.raw: "\n\n<i>“I knew you’d ask about that sooner or later."

rows.original: A lot of people do, although it’s usually just tourists, and you...” he glances at your treated physique, “you’re no newcomer.
rows.translation: 很多人都会问，虽然通常只有游客才问。而你...”他看了一眼你经过改造的体格，“你可不像新来的。
rows.raw: " A lot of people do, although it’s usually just tourists, and you...” he glances at your treated physique, “you’re no newcomer."

rows.original: Everyone wants to know the changes before they take it themselves.
rows.translation: 每个人亲自接受疗程前，都想知道会发生什么变化。
rows.raw: " Everyone wants to know the changes before they take it themselves."

rows.original: Well, The Treatment was originally a fertility drug administered to the initial immigrants who landed on this here planet, used to boost the population to colonize and fight against what Big T. calls ‘Mega Varmints’. After we got control of the planet a few... scratch that. A buncha people took a liking to The Treatment, soft women, strong men, was pretty natural to ‘em. The details around this time are a little fuzzy for me, but fast forward a couple generations and now it’s sunk into our genes, mandatory on our 18th birthday, and better than ever.”
rows.translation: 嗯，改造疗程最初是一种生育药物，用在最早登陆这颗星球的移民身上，通过增加人口来殖民，并对抗大T所谓的‘巨型害兽’。等我们控制住这颗星球，又过了几年...不对，有一大群人喜欢上了改造疗程带来的结果，柔软的女人、强壮的男人，这对他们来说很自然。那个时期的具体细节我记不太清了，不过快进几代之后，它已经融入了我们的基因，人人都必须在十八岁生日接受疗程，而且效果比以往更好。”
rows.raw: " Well, The Treatment was originally a fertility drug administered to the initial immigrants who landed on this here planet, used to boost the population to colonize and fight against what Big T. calls ‘Mega Varmints’. After we got control of the planet a few... scratch that. A buncha people took a liking to The Treatment, soft women, strong men, was pretty natural to ‘em. The details around this time are a little fuzzy for me, but fast forward a couple generations and now it’s sunk into our genes, mandatory on our 18th birthday, and better than ever.”"

rows.original: “And what about you? Were you always the hulking slab of meat you are today?” You ask sarcastically, underestimating the power of the Treatment.
rows.translation: “那你呢？你一直都是如今这块魁梧的肉山吗？”你用讽刺的语气问道，低估了改造疗程的威力。
rows.raw: "\n\n“And what about you? Were you always the hulking slab of meat you are today?” You ask sarcastically, underestimating the power of the Treatment."

rows.original: <i>“Actually, I was quite the nerd. Glasses, thin, nose-deep in books, no muscle bulk. Nothin’. But then once I got the Treatment at the beginning of my Senior school year things turned out much better for me. You see, before my Treating I was... close with the football team.
rows.translation: <i>“其实，我以前相当书呆子气。戴眼镜、身材瘦弱，整天埋头书本，没有一点肌肉。什么都没有。但在毕业年级开学时接受改造疗程后，一切都变得好多了。你看，接受疗程以前，我和橄榄球队...关系很密切。
rows.raw: "\n\n<i>“Actually, I was quite the nerd. Glasses, thin, nose-deep in books, no muscle bulk. Nothin’. But then once I got the Treatment at the beginning of my Senior school year things turned out much better for me. You see, before my Treating I was... close with the football team."

rows.original: I had a huge submissive streak. Whenever the cheerleaders were away I’d help the team get their rocks off; can’t let your boys play while pent up right? I never could bear to watch them suffer.
rows.translation: 我有很强的服从倾向。啦啦队不在的时候，我会帮球队发泄；总不能让兄弟们憋着上场，对吧？我一直不忍心看他们难受。
rows.raw: " I had a huge submissive streak. Whenever the cheerleaders were away I’d help the team get their rocks off; can’t let your boys play while pent up right? I never could bear to watch them suffer."

rows.original: Anyway, their Quarterback had a bad run in with The Treatment; turned him into a Faux-Cow,” you raise an eyebrow at Busky and he explains.
rows.translation: 总之，他们的四分卫接受改造疗程时出了岔子，变成了伪牛。”你朝巴斯基挑起眉毛，于是他解释道。
rows.raw: " Anyway, their Quarterback had a bad run in with The Treatment; turned him into a Faux-Cow,” you raise an eyebrow at Busky and he explains."

rows.original: <i>“A Faux-Cow is a male who took The Treatment, but lost muscle mass, and masculine traits. They also tend to be much more submissive, however they’re still male. Hence the ‘Faux’. And since I was so, er, close with the football team, and I had the same build the old quarterback had, I was the best choice for a replacement.
rows.translation: <i>“伪牛是接受了改造疗程，却失去肌肉量和男性特征的男人。他们通常也会变得更顺从，不过依然是男性。所以才叫‘伪’。而我和橄榄球队关系那么，呃，密切，又有着和那位旧四分卫相同的体格，自然成了最适合的替代人选。
rows.raw: "\n\n<i>“A Faux-Cow is a male who took The Treatment, but lost muscle mass, and masculine traits. They also tend to be much more submissive, however they’re still male. Hence the ‘Faux’. And since I was so, er, close with the football team, and I had the same build the old quarterback had, I was the best choice for a replacement."

rows.original: It also helped me relieve them after practice. Poor boys were always so pent up, I had to take care of them in the showers just to wash it all away.
rows.translation: 这也方便我在训练后替他们纾解。可怜的兄弟们总是憋得太难受，我不得不在淋浴间照顾他们，正好把一切都冲干净。
rows.raw: " It also helped me relieve them after practice. Poor boys were always so pent up, I had to take care of them in the showers just to wash it all away."

rows.original: <i>“Nowadays if I’m not here in the shop I’m at the gym, bulking up
rows.translation: <i>“现在，如果我不在店里，就会去健身房增肌
rows.raw: "\n\n<i>“Nowadays if I’m not here in the shop I’m at the gym, bulking up"

rows.original: , taking nostalgic showers if you know what I mean,
rows.translation: ，再洗个令人怀念的澡，你懂我的意思，
rows.raw: ", taking nostalgic showers if you know what I mean,"

rows.original: and maintaining this body. Not planning on going back to being a twig any time soon.”
rows.translation: 并保持这副身材。我暂时可不打算变回一根细竹竿。”
rows.raw: " and maintaining this body. Not planning on going back to being a twig any time soon.”"

rows.original: “Hey kid, if you’re looking for someone to spot ya, I gotcha,” Busky says, planting a firm hand on your shoulder, as if to show his reliability. “But yeah, I’ve kept this body in check for this long, I could probably do the same for you.
rows.translation: “嘿，小家伙，如果你需要有人保护，我可以帮你，”巴斯基一只结实的手搭上你的肩膀，仿佛在证明自己的可靠。“总之，我把这副身体维持到现在，可能也能替你做到同样的事。
rows.raw: "“Hey kid, if you’re looking for someone to spot ya, I gotcha,” Busky says, planting a firm hand on your shoulder, as if to show his reliability. “But yeah, I’ve kept this body in check for this long, I could probably do the same for you."

rows.original: And, if you’re ever looking for a spa buddy, we could spend a few hours in there.
rows.translation: 而且，如果你哪天想找个水疗伙伴，我们可以在那里待上几小时。
rows.raw: " And, if you’re ever looking for a spa buddy, we could spend a few hours in there."

rows.original: I know I ordered a shipment of muscle packing mods a while back. They’re probably still going through customs or somethin’, but once I get them, we’ll take them for a test at the gym.
rows.translation: 我记得前阵子订过一批增加肌肉的模组。它们大概还在过海关之类的地方，不过等收到货后，我们可以带去健身房试试。

rows.original: So it is you find yourself gliding through the air above the plains of New Texas with the windows rolled down, wind blowing [pc.hasLongHair|through|over] your [pc.hair], the twins excitedly chattering in the back. From fifty feet up, you really do get a sense of how monotone the landscape is; just grass, dirt, the occasional mesa, and huge, remorselessly even farms as far as the eye can see. The notion that time was brought to a standstill on this planet is intensified by seeing it from the air. The odd bloom of woodland really stands out, which is why, a couple hours out from New T’s ranch, the much coveted waterhole is not difficult to spot. You set the hovercab down with a wheeze at the edge of the trees: hybrid Terran oaks, willows and beeches, regal old growth. There’s a wonderfully cool balm to be found underneath their boughs, aided by the large, rocky pool you find nestled near the middle. It’s fed by a spring with a stream chattering away into the undergrowth off to one side. It appears completely deserted, although the existence of a tire swing on the steepest bank tells you that the locals are aware of it. Sunlight glints off the surface, and avian life twitters and sings in the branches. It might be heaven. The girls ferry their stuff from the hovercab trunk, pale yellow dresses swishing, chattering frenetically the whole time. In due course there are towels, a big cooler of food and drink, a little floating audio drone, a beachball, sunscreen, and holo devices arrayed on the gravelly shore. Let’s have some fun!” You put on your [pc.underGarments] before slipping into the cool water, and it is indeed wonderful against the hot, dry heat of New Texan air. You grow accustomed to the chill and splash around with the pair of them for a while, exulting in being all alone in this lush spot. After a bit, though, you decide to diversify your fun.
rows.translation: 于是，你就这样摇下车窗，驾驶悬浮出租车滑翔在新德克萨斯的平原上空，风吹[pc.hasLongHair|穿|过]你的[pc.hair]，双胞胎在后座兴奋地聊个不停。从五十英尺高处望去，这片景色是何等单调一目了然；放眼所及，只有草地、泥土、偶尔冒出的台地，以及巨大得无情而整齐的农场。从空中俯瞰，更让人觉得这颗星球的时间仿佛停滞不前。零星绽开的林地格外醒目，因此离开新·T的牧场几小时后，那处人人垂涎的水潭并不难找。 你让悬浮出租车喘息着降落在树林边缘：地球橡树、柳树与山毛榉的杂交品种，都是庄严的古老大树。枝叶下有一片美妙清凉的荫蔽，林地中央附近嵌着一座岩石环绕的大水潭，更添凉意。泉水汇入其中，一条小溪在一侧潺潺流入灌木丛。这里似乎完全无人，只有最陡河岸上的轮胎秋千说明当地人知道这个地方。 阳光在水面闪烁，鸟儿在枝头啁啾歌唱。这里或许就是天堂。 姑娘们从悬浮出租车的后备箱搬出东西，淡黄色裙摆摇曳，全程都在飞快地叽叽喳喳。不久，砾石岸边便摆满了毛巾、一大冷藏箱食物和饮料、一台漂浮音频无人机、一个沙滩球、防晒霜和全息设备。她们脱下宽松的裙子，露出两件式比基尼——凯莉的是浅蓝色，科拉的是深红色，两件都几乎兜不住她们乳白颤动的曲线——随后把脚趾探进水里，抽动着发出咕咕声与轻笑。 “这不是很棒吗，大[pc.guy]?”凯莉冲你灿烂一笑。“来嘛！咱们好好玩玩！” 你穿上[pc.underGarments]，随后滑入清凉的水中；在新德克萨斯炎热干燥的空气里，这感觉的确美妙。你逐渐适应凉意，和她们俩嬉水了一阵，尽情享受独占这片葱郁天地的感觉。不过过了一会儿，你决定换点别的乐子。
rows.raw: " So it is you find yourself gliding through the air above the plains of New Texas with the windows rolled down, wind blowing [pc.hasLongHair|through|over] your [pc.hair], the twins excitedly chattering in the back. From fifty feet up, you really do get a sense of how monotone the landscape is; just grass, dirt, the occasional mesa, and huge, remorselessly even farms as far as the eye can see. The notion that time was brought to a standstill on this planet is intensified by seeing it from the air. The odd bloom of woodland really stands out, which is why, a couple hours out from New T’s ranch, the much coveted waterhole is not difficult to spot. You set the hovercab down with a wheeze at the edge of the trees: hybrid Terran oaks, willows and beeches, regal old growth. There’s a wonderfully cool balm to be found underneath their boughs, aided by the large, rocky pool you find nestled near the middle. It’s fed by a spring with a stream chattering away into the undergrowth off to one side. It appears completely deserted, although the existence of a tire swing on the steepest bank tells you that the locals are aware of it. Sunlight glints off the surface, and avian life twitters and sings in the branches. It might be heaven. The girls ferry their stuff from the hovercab trunk, pale yellow dresses swishing, chattering frenetically the whole time. In due course there are towels, a big cooler of food and drink, a little floating audio drone, a beachball, sunscreen, and holo devices arrayed on the gravelly shore. They shuck off their billowy dresses, revealing their two-piece bikinis — Carrie’s is a light blue, Cora’s is crimson, both barely up to the task of containing their milky, quivering curves — and dip their toes in the water with twitching coos and giggles. “Isn’t this wonderful, big [pc.guy]?” Carrie turns a big grin on you. “C’mon! Let’s have some fun!” You put on your [pc.underGarments] before slipping into the cool water, and it is indeed wonderful against the hot, dry heat of New Texan air. You grow accustomed to the chill and splash around with the pair of them for a while, exulting in being all alone in this lush spot. After a bit, though, you decide to diversify your fun. "

rows.original: You break away from the girls for a little bit, enjoying the feeling of water coursing over your [pc.skinFurScales] as you slowly paddle around the periphery of the pool, exploring the deeper end where the stream leads off, diving beneath the surface. It’s there you feel something nibble your [pc.foot]. Oh! There’s fish! “Yeah, there’s lots actually,” Cora replies when you call out. “Don’t worry though, they’re harmless.” “Sometimes the guys come and do a lil bit of fishing,” Carrie says. “I think one of my uncles left his rod ‘n tackle in the cooler, actually...” “Noo, don’t tell [pc.him] that Carrie!” Cora splashes her sister. “[pc.He]’ll want to do that and it’s soooo boring!” You consider the flicker of gold and silver in the particulate-suspended gloom beneath your [pc.feet]. You could try your luck with a rod. How often are you able to fish on an alien planet? It’s likely to irk your attention-craving companions, though.
rows.translation: 你暂时离开姑娘们，慢慢划过水潭边缘，享受水流淌过[pc.skinFurScales]的感觉。你来到小溪流出的深水区，潜入水面之下。就在这里，你感觉有什么东西啃了啃你的[pc.foot]。哦！有鱼！ “对呀，其实有很多，”你喊出声后，科拉回答。“不过别担心，它们不会伤人。” “有时候男人们会来钓一小会儿鱼，”凯莉说道。“其实我觉得有个叔叔把他的鱼竿和渔具留在冷藏箱里了...” “不——别告诉[pc.him]这个，凯莉！”科拉朝姐姐泼水。“[pc.He]会想去钓鱼的，那也太——无聊了！” 你望着[pc.feet]下方、悬浮微粒造成的昏暗水色中闪动的金银光芒。你可以拿鱼竿试试运气。你又有多少机会能在外星球钓鱼呢？不过这样很可能会惹恼两位渴望你关注的同伴。

rows.original: [var0 |Ignoring the groans of female exasperation, you head back to the cooler and retrieve the collapsible fishing rod stashed in the bottom. It’s a simple, synthetic, traditional affair with a wire line, red sinker and (of course) a horn-shaped hook. You break off some hard cheese from a sandwich, stick it on the hook, then send it whirring out over the glittering surface of the pool, towards where you think you saw the largest concentration of fish. |“You aren’t gunna be boring, are you big [pc.guy]?” says Carrie with a slightly plaintive flutter of her eyelashes, as you head towards the cooler. “[pc.he] is... ah bullcakes, [pc.he] is,” groans Cora, flopping dramatically back on the pebble beach as you retrieve the fishing gear from the bottom. “I keep tellin’ you to take that damn rod outta there!” You stoically ignore their complaints. You’ll make it up to them later. You don’t get to do this anywhere else; and the sunlit peace here, with its gentle sound of water, it’s perfect for slipping in a meditative state while you watch a bright red float bob on the waves. And, just, maybe, you’ll get a bite. Whizzzzzzzzz! ]
rows.translation: [var0 |你无视女人们恼怒的抱怨，回到冷藏箱旁，取出藏在底部的折叠鱼竿。这是一套简单的合成材质传统渔具，带金属线、红色沉子，以及一个（当然了）角状鱼钩。你从三明治上掰下一块硬奶酪，挂到鱼钩上，随后让钓线呼啸着飞过闪闪发光的水面，落向你认为鱼群最密集的地方。 |“你不会真要这么无聊吧，大[pc.guy]?”你走向冷藏箱时，凯莉眨着睫毛，略带哀求地说道。 “[pc.he]就是...啊，真是牛胡扯，[pc.he]就是要钓，”科拉呻吟着，夸张地向后倒在卵石滩上，而你从箱底取出渔具。 “我一直叫你把那根该死的鱼竿拿出去！” 你坚忍地无视她们的抱怨。稍后会补偿她们的。你在别处可没有这样的机会；这里阳光明媚、流水轻响、宁静祥和，正适合望着鲜红浮标随波起伏，进入冥想状态。 而且，也许，就那么一下，你会有鱼上钩。嗖嗖嗖嗖嗖嗖嗖嗖！ ]

rows.original: [var0 |You are shaken out of a sun-kissed doze by the rod tugging in your hands. A bite! A bite! You take hold of the rod and, by luck or by crook, manage to guide the struggling fish to where your net and hands await it. It’s a [var2|Spotted Grout! Admire its black speckles and astoundingly ugly face.|Blue Steerpike! See its glittering scales and ropy body.|Pale Alito! Look at its ruminative whiskers and plate-like body.|Golden Fanfin? You didn’t even know you could find them in New Texas. See its diva-like fins and shimmering, shifting scales!] [var1 |Even your companions forget they’re supposed to be annoyed with you when you show them, cooing over your remarkable catch. “Take it to Smee’s, [pc.name]!” Carrie says. “You can find him in the spaceport, he pays for catches o’ the day. He’s an expert on fishy stuff, he’ll be really interested in this! |Your companions are not quite as enthused as you are by your catch, even less so when you insist room in the cooler must be made for it, but you’re so chuffed with yourself you don’t really care. [flags.SMEE_APPROACH |You should take it to Soggybottom Smee’s before you leave. |Maybe there’s somewhere on New Texas you could take it for appraisal? ] ] |An hour trickles by without incident. The float bobs on the surface, undisturbed. You might doze off in the dappled sunlight, although you assure the twins, whenever they inquire, that you’re paying very close attention to your line. Regardless of your level of concentration, your bait fails to get the attention of any of the quicksilver creatures in the murk. “Done wastin’ your time?” pouts Cora, when you return the rod. You assure them that fishing is not about catching fish, not at all; it’s about communing with a body of natural water. The timeless, contemplative state you slip in by a riverside in the sun. You aren’t terribly convincing. ]

rows.original: Inevitably, your eye is drawn to the tire swing. It’s not in fact a tire — you hazard it’s a piece of protective tubing from one of those massive farm crawlers you saw from the hovercab, tied roughly into a loop — but the principle is the same. You charge at it, grabbing and using the momentum to fling yourself out over an eight foot drop, hanging in the air for an exhilarating moment, and then come splashing down.[pc.isHeight 72|| It was strung up by and for bulls, which means poor little you has to take a big run up and really jump at it in order to make it pitch. It’s so worth it, though.] The twins giggle and cheer the first time you soak them with one of your cannonballs. The third and fourth time, not so much. “Stooop it,” Carrie whines, splashing at you when you emerge fountaining cool water again. Ok, you probably should... but then the swing catches your eye again, like the seductive minx it is. You can’t help but think you haven’t experienced it to its fullest potential. Like, if you charged at it flat out, and let go right at the apex of the swing, you would be flung right over the two girls paddling around beneath, not catching them with any spray at all (probably)! It would be incredibly impressive.
rows.translation: 你的目光不可避免地被轮胎秋千吸引过去。它其实并不是轮胎；你猜那是从悬浮出租车上见过的某种巨型农用履带车的防护管，被人粗略地绑成了环状；不过原理都一样。你朝它冲过去，一把抓住，借着冲势把自己荡向八英尺高的落差之外，在空中刺激地悬停片刻，随后哗啦一声落进水里。[pc.isHeight 72||它是由公牛们架起来、也是给公牛们玩的，所以可怜又娇小的你必须远远助跑，再使劲跃起才能让它荡起来。不过这一切绝对值得。] 你第一次用炮弹式跳水把双胞胎浇得浑身湿透时，她们还咯咯笑着为你欢呼。到了第三次和第四次，她们就没那么开心了。 “别闹啦，”凯莉抱怨道；当你再次带着喷泉般的凉水冒出来时，她朝你泼起水来。 好吧，你大概确实该停手了...可那架秋千又勾住了你的目光，活像个勾人的小妖精。你忍不住觉得，自己还没把它的潜力彻底发挥出来。比如说，如果你全速冲向它，在秋千荡到最高点的那一刻松手，你就会直接飞过下方划水的两个女孩，完全不会溅到她们身上（大概吧）！那肯定会无比惊艳。

rows.original: Oh, tire swing... you’re so bad for [pc.name], but [pc.he] just can’t say no to you, can [pc.he]? You slip away from the girls, supposedly to fetch something from the hovercab, then scoot quietly up the slope to where the worn ring and rope await. You rub your hands, take a deep breath... then charge at it as fast as you can. You swing up in the air, the rough rubber leaves your hands, and then you are flying, flying... there’s a breathless scream from somewhere... but you are alone with the air, a state of ecstatic simplicity... rows.original: You fetch the colorful inflatable and bop it towards one of the twins, who punches it to the other with a gleeful moo. The game is to keep the ball in the air while staying afloat, which someone who is more accustomed to fighting feral aliens out on the untamed frontier is obviously not going to lose. The wholesome activity does have a slight twist to it though, since every time one of the cowgirls reaches up to bop the ball away, their own... in-built flotation devices... bounce. Generously and exuberantly. Obviously you know what those look like, but there’s something specifically about the Treated which make them impossible not to ogle. You can’t help your eyes being drawn to those mountains of jiggling, creamy flesh, cold water keeping their plump nipples hard beneath the thin, shifting fabric of their bikinis, strings heroically taut against the heavy, supple weight of... ...the ball bops you on the forehead. High-pitched giggling rings around the clearing. “What’s the matter, big [pc.boy]? It’s a simple game! Can’t you concentrate?” “[pc.His] tongue is practically danglin’ out!” “Aww. Don’t be mean to [pc.him], sis.” Carrie pulls herself to her sister’s side, smiling at you as she presses her boob into Cora’s shoulder, plumping the pale softness outwards. “[pc.He] can’t help keepin’ [pc.his] eyes on what really matters, can [pc.he]?” You don’t think they minded your eyes drifting much.
rows.translation: 你拿来色彩鲜艳的充气球，把它拍向双胞胎之一；她欢快地哞叫一声，又把球击向另一人。游戏规则是在自己浮在水上的同时不让球落下；一个习惯在蛮荒边疆对付野生外星人的人，显然不可能输掉这种比赛。不过这项健康活动也稍微有点特别，因为每当一个牛姑娘抬手击球，她们自带的...漂浮装置...便会跟着弹跳。慷慨而又欢腾。当然，你知道那些东西是什么样子，但改造者身上就是有某种特质，让人无法不去盯着看。你的视线忍不住被那两座颤动的乳白肉山吸引；冰冷潭水让她们丰满的乳头在轻薄移位的比基尼布料下保持坚挺，系带英勇地绷在那沉甸甸而又柔软的重量之下... ...球砸中了你的额头。高亢的咯咯笑声回荡在林间空地。 “怎么了，大[pc.boy]?游戏很简单呀！你就不能专心吗？” “[pc.His]舌头都快垂出来了！” “噢。别欺负[pc.him]，姐姐。”凯莉游到姐姐身边，微笑着把乳房压在科拉肩上，将苍白柔软的乳肉挤向外侧。“[pc.He]忍不住让[pc.his]目光一直盯着真正重要的东西，[pc.he]说对不对？” 你觉得她们大概并不介意你的目光四处游移。

rows.original: “We should eat,” Carrie says, a short time later. “While the food’s still fresh.” You walk back up onto the rocky beach and towel yourself down, watching as the cowgirl pulls the cooler open and unloads a remarkable amount of food. A pitcher of juice, chicken legs, homemade pie, some kind of plump yellow fruit, cheese sandwiches... the cheese is, uh, where does the cheese come from...?
rows.translation: “我们该吃东西了，”过了一会儿，凯莉说道。“趁食物还新鲜。” 你走回岩石岸边，用毛巾擦干身体，看着牛姑娘打开冷藏箱，拿出数量惊人的食物。一壶果汁、鸡腿、自制馅饼、某种饱满的黄色水果、奶酪三明治...呃，奶酪是从哪里来的...?

rows.original: “Tuck in,” Carrie smiles. “I’m gonna sunbathe first,” Cora says, laying out a towel in a splash of sunshine and undoing her top. “Leave some for me, k?” It’s only when you bite into the first sandwich that you realize how hungry you are. There’s nothing quite like wild swimming to work up an appetite. You find yourself bulldozing your way through the picnic spread while Cora just plain dozes, rested on top of her boobs, bonnet of fiery hair down, gentle curve of her back bared to New Texas’s sun.
rows.translation: “尽管吃，”凯莉微笑道。 “我要先晒会儿太阳，”科拉说道。她把毛巾铺在一片阳光中，解开上衣。“给我留点，好吗？” 直到咬下第一口三明治，你才意识到自己有多饿。没有什么比野外游泳更能激起食欲。你风卷残云般横扫野餐食物，而科拉干脆打起了瞌睡，趴在自己的乳房上，火红头发披散下来，背部柔和的曲线裸露在新德克萨斯的阳光下。

rows.original: You can’t help it. And you’re the ‘big [pc.guy]’, right? You need your protein. And vitamin C. And carbs. And... “You ate the whole darn thing,” Cora says, as cool and stony as the beach you’re sitting on, turning the cooler upside down about fifteen minutes later. “I wanted to stop [pc.him], but... it was kinda incredible to watch,” Carrie offers with a nervous giggle. “I guess you really like my cookin’, huh [pc.name]?” “So do I.” Cora is looking at you with the expression of a cow that has very particular opinions about her paddock, one of which is that you don’t belong in it. In for a credit, in for a slave — you’ll just say it...she needn’t worry, because you intend for her to leave here VERY full. “You should be so gosh-darn lucky!” Cora cries in outrage, tail swishing furiously as Carrie falls about in helpless giggles. “You ain’t a bull, you’re a pig!” Well, whatever. It’s difficult to feel too repentant when you’re also feeling as content as you currently do. Homemade, homegrown New Texan cuisine: simple, good, filling.
rows.translation: 你实在忍不住。而且你是“大[pc.guy]”，对吧？你需要蛋白质。还需要维生素C。还需要碳水化合物。还有... “你把该死的东西全吃光了，”大约十五分钟后，科拉把冷藏箱倒过来，语气像你坐着的岸边一样冰冷坚硬。 “我本来想阻止[pc.him]，可是...看着还挺不可思议的，”凯莉紧张地咯咯笑道。“看来你真的很喜欢我做的饭，对吧，[pc.name]?” “我也喜欢。” 科拉看你的表情，就像一头对自己的牧场有着非常明确看法的母牛，其中一条便是你不该待在这里。既然已经花了一枚信用点，那就干脆买下整个奴隶——你索性直说了...她不用担心，因为你打算让她离开这里时吃得非常“饱”。 “你想得倒美！”科拉愤怒地大叫，尾巴疯狂甩动，凯莉则无力地笑倒在一旁。“你才不是公牛，你是头猪！” 好吧，随她怎么说。当你像现在这样心满意足时，实在很难生出多少悔意。自家烹饪、自家种植的新德克萨斯料理：简单、美味、饱腹。

rows.original: Putting the homemade food to one side is tough, but weighed against the equally sensual enjoyment of sun-warmed cowgirl, it’s not so bad. You wash your hands, scoot over to where Cora is lying, and tell her she needs some more sunscreen. “No I don’t,” she murmurs. “But... ooh,” she sighs, as you rub your lotion-slathered hands together and then apply them to her smooth, hot back. “Ummm... yes, you can keep doing that.” You don’t need to be any kind of experienced masseuse to make a cowgirl purr; you just need the tiniest amount of patience and to be reasonably gentle. It only takes a few sweeps of your oily hands up the curve of Cora’s back, neck, and upper arms, feeling her slender muscles under her soft, supple flesh, to make her fall into something like a sensual coma, groaning, sighing and then mooing quietly, auburn tail-puff flicking dreamily. You let your fingers roam a little more, pulling her swimsuit down a bit so the swell of her juicy backside can receive some much needed manual attention — and no complaint is registered from you doing so. “Do me next!” Carrie says brightly, laying herself down beside her sister. “Moooo,” she’s groaning about a minute later as you varnish her pale skin to a shine. “Around my shoulders... oh that’s it... moooo!” “ -nk you f’r leavin’ s-m f’r mme,” Cora chews, a little later still. The dilated pupils and goofy, happy grins the pair of them are turning on you now say thank you much clearer. Such tactile creatures.
rows.translation: 要把自制美食搁到一边实在很难，但若和享用被阳光晒暖的牛女郎那同样充满感官诱惑的乐趣相比，倒也没那么糟。你洗干净双手，挪到科拉躺着的地方，告诉她还得再涂些防晒霜。 “我才不需要，”她低声说道。“不过...哦，”你将沾满乳液的双手互相揉搓，随后按上她光滑滚烫的后背，她不禁叹息起来。“嗯...对，你可以继续。” 想让一位牛女郎舒服得哼哼出声，你根本不需要当什么经验丰富的按摩师；只需有那么一点耐心，动作也足够轻柔就行。你油润的双手只在科拉弧线优美的背部、颈项和上臂来回抚过几遍，感受柔软嫩肉下的纤细肌肉，她便陷入某种感官昏迷般的状态，先是呻吟、叹息，随后低声哞叫，赤褐色的尾巴绒球也如梦似幻地轻轻甩动。你让手指游走得更远了些，把她的泳装往下拉了一点，好让她丰润后臀的隆起接受亟需的手工照料；你这么做也没有招来任何抗议。 “接下来给我按！”凯莉兴高采烈地说道，在姐姐身旁趴下。大约一分钟后，当你把她苍白的肌肤抹得油亮发光时，她已经在呻吟：“哞——”“肩膀周围...哦，就是那里...哞——！” “谢、谢谢你还给我留了点，”又过了一会儿，科拉一边咀嚼一边含糊说道。如今她们两人望向你时，那放大的瞳孔和傻乎乎的幸福笑容，已经把谢意表达得更加清楚。真是喜欢身体接触的生物。

rows.original: You spread your own towel down near Cora and lay your [pc.skinFurScales] out under Nye’s hot, unblinking gaze. It’s nice, after a bit of exercise and a meal, just to lie here, listening to the gentle lap of water over the pebblestone beach nearby... indeed, it’s very, very nice... [var0 |You blink and shake your head just as you feel yourself sinking towards the land of Nod. Close thing — your [pc.skin] is feeling very toasty now. The cool water glimmers invitingly. |“[pc.name]!” “Wakey wakey big [pc.guy]!” You come to with a jerk. Oh Void... you must have fallen asleep! The twins are giggling at you, and you feel your cheeks burn. It’s more than just embarrassment. You touch your [pc.skin] and wince: New Texas’s sun has reminded you that it is, indeed, a gigantic radioactive explosion. “Shush shush, it ain’t so bad,” tuts Carrie as she rubs the aftersun she thankfully remembered to bring over your roasted shoulders, neck and [pc.ears]. “Maybe it’ll learn you to be a lil more careful next time, huh sleepyhead?” Yeah. Certainly the cool water is looking mighty inviting right now. ]

[var0 |就在感觉自己即将沉入梦乡时，你眨眨眼，摇了摇头。好险——你的[pc.skin]现在已经烤得很热。清凉水面诱人地闪着光。 |“[pc.name]!” “醒醒，大[pc.guy]!” 你猛地惊醒。虚空啊...你肯定睡着了！双胞胎冲你咯咯笑，你感觉双颊发烫。这不只是因为尴尬。你碰了碰[pc.skin]，痛得缩了一下：新德克萨斯的太阳提醒你，它的确是一场巨大的放射性爆炸。 “好啦好啦，没那么糟，”凯莉咂嘴说道，把她幸好记得带来的晒后修复霜涂在你晒伤的肩膀、脖子和[pc.ears]上。“也许这能让你下次小心一点，对吧，小瞌睡虫？” 是啊。此刻那片清凉潭水看起来确实无比诱人。 ]

rows.original: [var0 |The varmint is pretty damn big. But you appear even bigger when you raise your arms and yell at it as loud as you can, charging out of the water towards it like an outraged hippopotamus as you do. The beast hisses, spines quivering. For a moment you think it’s going to stand its ground... and then it’s turning tail, making good its escape into the trees, its odd, metallic barks fading into the distance. “Yeah! Go on, git!” “Yeah! Wooowww! Our hero!” You are presently sandwiched between two cooing cowgirls, looking up at you with wide, worshipful eyes as they shower you with praise. Your [pc.chest] swells; you slide your arms around their waists and give them a joint, comforting squeeze. It was nothing, really... you just have to show these animals who’s the boss. “Well, that’s you alright!” Carrie bats her lashes at you and leans forward, so you can get a gigantic eyeful of her cleavage. “The boss.” You are handfed the little yellow fruit in the relieved, idyllic picnic that follows. You begin to feel like some kind of ancient woodland god[pc.mf||dess], spending an afternoon in a secluded grove with some delightful nymphs. It is not the worst feeling in the galaxy. |Without another thought, you charge yelling out of the water towards the varmint. It’s when it turns towards you and bares its nail-sized fangs, raises its equally sharp spines, that you have a second thought. It makes your cry falter in your throat. The varmint bounds towards you, snarling like tortured metal. Oh no, oh fuck, oh void... you are forced to beat a retreat back into the water, hoping that the things are not swimmers. Whether they are or not, the giant lizard seems to feel it’s made its point by herding you into the deeps. It trots back up towards the food. You and the cowgirls are forced to watch as it helps itself, ignoring the carbon-based chicken in favor of the fruit, pie, and salad, before eating the cooler itself. Only then does it mosey off. “You were supposed to scare ‘em off!” You’re feeling beat enough without having to hear this too, but hear it you must. You slump down on your towel as the twins march back down the beach to berate you. “It took me half a day to make all that food!” “What use is a big [pc.guy] if [pc.he] can’t even shoo a titchy lil varmint off?!” “WE’RE havin’ the chicken. If you want somethin’ to eat, you kin go hunt that thing down like a real bull would!” This hardly seems fair, but you suppose you have to accept the downsides of the machismic role you’ve adopted around these two, and you go hungry with a show of stoicism. At least after they’ve feasted on the drumsticks Carrie and Cora are a little more content. ]
rows.translation: [var0 |这只害兽大得要命。但当你高举双臂，拼尽全力冲它吼叫，像一头愤怒的河马般从水里朝它冲去时，你显得更加庞大。 野兽嘶嘶作响，棘刺颤动。有那么一瞬间，你以为它会守住阵地...接着它却转身逃跑，钻进树林，古怪的金属吠声逐渐消失在远方。 “对！快滚吧！” “对！哇啊啊！我们的英雄！” 你随即被两个咕咕叫的牛姑娘夹在中间。她们用崇拜的大眼睛仰望着你，不停赞美。[pc.chest]得意地挺起；你双臂环住她们的腰，同时安慰地搂紧两人。其实没什么...只需要让这些动物知道谁才是老大。 “没错，你就是老大！”凯莉眨着睫毛向前倾身，让你把她的乳沟尽收眼底。“老大。” 在随后轻松而田园诗般的野餐中，她们亲手把黄色小果子喂给你。你开始觉得自己像某种古老的林中神祇[pc.mf||女神]，与几位可爱的宁芙在隐秘林地里度过午后。这绝不是银河系里最糟糕的感觉。 |你不假思索地大喊着冲出水面，奔向害兽。当它转身面对你，露出指甲大小的尖牙，又竖起同样锋利的棘刺时，你才产生了第二个念头。你的喊声卡在喉咙里。 害兽朝你猛扑，咆哮声如同受折磨的金属。哦不，操，虚空啊...你被迫撤回水中，希望这种东西不会游泳。 无论它会不会游泳，这只巨蜥似乎觉得把你赶进深水已经表明了态度。它小跑回食物旁。你和牛姑娘们只能眼睁睁看着它大吃起来；它无视以碳为基础的鸡肉，转而吃掉水果、馅饼和沙拉，最后连冷藏箱本身都吃了。然后它才慢悠悠地离开。 “你本来应该把它赶走的！” 你已经够受打击了，根本不想再听这些，可你又不得不听。双胞胎沿岸边走回来责骂你时，你瘫坐在毛巾上。 “我花了半天才做好那些食物！” “大[pc.guy]要是[pc.he]连一只小小的害兽都赶不走，那还有什么用？!” “鸡肉归我们吃。你要想吃东西，就像真正的公牛那样去猎杀那玩意儿！” 这似乎很不公平，但既然你在她们俩面前扮演了这种大男子主义角色，大概就得接受坏处。你故作坚忍地饿着肚子。至少凯莉和科拉吃完鸡腿后，心情好了一点。 ]

rows.original: You beckon the twins to be quiet, and wait in the water for the varmint to leave. Leave it does, but not before consuming all of the picnic aside from the chicken, as well as the cooler itself. It makes a noise like an exhaust backfiring, which you suppose is its equivalent of a belch, and then bounds off into the trees. The girls are not happy. “You were supposed to scare ‘em off!” “It took me half a day to make all that food!” “What use is a big [pc.guy] if [pc.he] can’t even shoo a titchy lil varmint off?!” You roll your eyes at this barrage of criticism and tell them it was far safer to just let the creature have its way than to try and fend it off with no weapons. Do either of them have first aid training? Well then. “Well...” Carrie is still fuming a little. “...I still think a real bull would’ve at least tried.” Taking charge of the situation in some way helped a bit you think, and after they’ve had what remains, they mellowed out some.
rows.translation: 你示意双胞胎保持安静，和她们一起待在水里等那只害兽离开。它确实走了，但临走前吃光了野餐中除鸡肉外的所有食物，连冷藏箱本身也没放过。它发出一声排气管回火般的响动，你猜那相当于它打了个嗝，随后便蹦跳着钻进树林。 女孩们很不高兴。 “你本来应该把它赶走的！” “我花了半天才做好那些食物！” “一个大块头[pc.guy]连只丁点大的小害兽都赶不走，那要[pc.he]有什么用？！” 面对这一连串批评，你翻了个白眼，告诉她们：手无寸铁时，与其试着赶走那只生物，让它随心所欲反而安全得多。她们俩有人受过急救训练吗？既然没有，那就对了。 “可是...”凯莉仍有些气鼓鼓的。“...我还是觉得，真正的公牛至少会试一试。” 你觉得，以某种方式掌控局面多少起了点作用；吃完剩下的东西后，她们的情绪也缓和了一些。

rows.original: A dark, shaggy, wedge-shaped head about the size of an armchair has parted the foliage on the other side of the pool. It is crowned by sharp, prong-shaped horns that are each longer than your arms. Nostrils flare, billowing steam and mucus; a pale tongue like a giant fern leaf laps at the water. You suppose it’s a lot like a bison. A bison would quail in the shadow of this thing, however. “A-auroch...” someone whispers shrilly. The two cowgirls have taken cover in the bushes opposite. Both have turned the color of snow. “Do something, [pc.name]! It’ll eat the food!” You don’t think the creature is even aware of you currently. Behind brown, wet eyes the size of melons, an intelligence as slow and implacable as a glacier moves.

rows.original: You [pc.move] steadily towards the auroch in the shallows, [pc.chest] flung out, waiting until it can’t ignore you and must raise its giant head to mark your passage. You hold its eye, open your mouth - and make a noise you weren’t sure you were capable of making. A primordial ogre bellow from the same kind of ancient epoch the creature itself surely belongs to. You marry that with a charge that leaves all notions of fear and calculation in your slipstream; because if you flinch even for a moment - if it sees in your eyes that you don’t fully intend to fucking headbutt it into the next century - this will not work. The auroch watches you come with its mouth slightly ajar. If it just stands there then you’ll run into it as if it were a brick wall, with a similar sort of effect. At the last moment, it makes a low, booming sound, turns, and lumbers away. It’s like watching a hairy mountain flee. You stand with your [pc.legs] in the water, panting. Did - did you just do that? Judging by the slack expressions of the pair of cowgirls that join you a moment later, they don’t really believe it either. “An auroch...” breathes Cora. “I had no idea they came down from the mountains so far!” “You - you really did drive it off, huh big [pc.guy]?” Carrie turns awe-filled eyes on you. “Not even T would’ve tried that. You’re - you’re pretty incredible, you know that right?” “You know what? Let’s skip lunch. Let’s get to the part where we have sex. Or, you can eat lunch while we, y’know.” Cora puts her tongue in her cheek and makes an unsubtle gesture. She giggles a little, and then looks at you dead serious. “I - really need you to do me, right now. That was - unnmph.” You grab generous handfuls of soft cowgirl in both hands, laugh, and say all in due time. For now, you’re hungry. This has the desired effect of making the pair of them whine in frustration, then giggle and fawn over you. The picnic is... sticky. There’s a lot of licked fingers, groans of enjoyment, extended tongues, handfed fruit: carryings-on of that nature. By the time you’re satiated, [pc.eachCock] are throbbing and semi-hard with latent lust. Hell yes. Celebrating your incredible victory over the auroch by bonking a pair of red-headed bimbos into next week is a profoundly, primally satisfying idea.
rows.translation: 你挺起[pc.chest]，[pc.move]稳稳走向浅水中的原牛，等到它再也无法无视你，不得不抬起巨大的脑袋注视你的行动。你迎着它的目光，张开嘴——发出一种连自己都不知道能发出的声音。那是来自原始巨魔的咆哮，仿佛源自这只生物本身所属的远古时代。你随即发起冲锋，把所有恐惧和算计都抛在身后的气流中；因为只要你退缩哪怕一瞬——只要它从你眼里看出你并不是真的打算用脑袋把它撞进下个世纪——这一招便不会奏效。 原牛微张着嘴，看着你逼近。如果它就那么站着，你会像撞上一堵砖墙那样撞上它，结果大概也差不多。 最后一刻，它发出低沉轰鸣，转过身，拖着沉重身躯离开。看起来就像一座长毛的山正在逃跑。 你站在水里，[pc.legs]浸在其中，气喘吁吁。你、你刚才真的做到了？片刻后赶来的两个牛姑娘一脸呆滞，显然她们也难以置信。 “一头原牛...”科拉屏息说道。“我都不知道它们会从山上走这么远！” “你、你真的把它赶走了，对吧，大[pc.guy]?”凯莉满眼敬畏地看着你。“就连T也不敢这么做。你、你真的很了不起，你知道吧？” “知道吗？午餐先不吃了。直接进入做爱环节吧。或者，你可以一边吃午餐，我们一边，嗯，你懂的。”科拉用舌头顶着脸颊，做了个毫不隐晦的手势。她轻笑了一下，随后无比认真地看着你。“我、我现在真的需要你狠狠干我。刚才那一下，呃嗯。” 你两手各抓住一大把柔软的牛姑娘，笑着说一切都得按顺序来。现在你饿了。这句话如愿让她们俩沮丧地哀鸣，随后又咯咯笑着对你百般讨好。 这场野餐...黏糊糊的。舔过的手指、享受的呻吟、伸得长长的舌头、亲手喂来的水果：尽是诸如此类的举动。等你吃饱时，[pc.eachCock]已因潜藏的欲望而悸动着半勃。太棒了。把一对红发花瓶女狠狠干到下周，以庆祝你战胜原牛的惊人胜利，这个想法从深层原始本能上令人无比满足。
rows.raw: " You [pc.move] steadily towards the auroch in the shallows, [pc.chest] flung out, waiting until it can’t ignore you and must raise its giant head to mark your passage. You hold its eye, open your mouth - and make a noise you weren’t sure you were capable of making. A primordial ogre bellow from the same kind of ancient epoch the creature itself surely belongs to. You marry that with a charge that leaves all notions of fear and calculation in your slipstream; because if you flinch even for a moment - if it sees in your eyes that you don’t fully intend to fucking headbutt it into the next century - this will not work. The auroch watches you come with its mouth slightly ajar. If it just stands there then you’ll run into it as if it were a brick wall, with a similar sort of effect. At the last moment, it makes a low, booming sound, turns, and lumbers away. It’s like watching a hairy mountain flee. You stand with your [pc.legs] in the water, panting. Did - did you just do that? Judging by the slack expressions of the pair of cowgirls that join you a moment later, they don’t really believe it either. “An auroch...” breathes Cora. “I had no idea they came down from the mountains so far!” “You - you really did drive it off, huh big [pc.guy]?” Carrie turns awe-filled eyes on you. “Not even T would’ve tried that. You’re - you’re pretty incredible, you know that right?” “You know what? Let’s skip lunch. Let’s get to the part where we have sex. Or, you can eat lunch while we, y’know.” Cora puts her tongue in her cheek and makes an unsubtle gesture. She giggles a little, and then looks at you dead serious. “I - really need you to do me, right now. That was - unnmph.” You grab generous handfuls of soft cowgirl in both hands, laugh, and say all in due time. For now, you’re hungry. This has the desired effect of making the pair of them whine in frustration, then giggle and fawn over you. The picnic is... sticky. There’s a lot of licked fingers, groans of enjoyment, extended tongues, handfed fruit: carryings-on of that nature. By the time you’re satiated, [pc.eachCock] are throbbing and semi-hard with latent lust. Hell yes. Celebrating your incredible victory over the auroch by bonking a pair of red-headed bimbos into next week is a profoundly, primally satisfying idea. "

rows.original: You emerge from the water, [pc.moving] towards the auroch with your [pc.chest] flung out. The creature raises its desk-sized head to regard you with its wet, solemnly stupid eyes. “Shoo!” you yell. “Get out of here! This is our water hole, you — uh...” You have enough time to consider how puny your voice seems in the presence of this colossus — how small you might appear without any of your hostile environment gear — before the thing lowers its horns and charges with sudden, shocking speed, lip rearing back from yellowed piano key teeth, water exploding around its hooves. WHAM.

rows.original: The trees above do eventually stop spinning sickeningly, but the pain in your arm and side do not. Stretched out on a towel, Carrie and Cora fuss over you, using another towel as a makeshift sling for your arm and applying cool water to your forehead. You groan as Carrie gingerly moves your bicep around. “I don’t think it’s broken, but you should get a Joybot to have a look at it anyway. It’s gunna be a heck of a bruise at the very least... Co-co, has it really gone?” “Oh yeah. It got all the water it needed after it, uh... yeah.” “That was very brave of you, [pc.name],” Carrie sighs, shaking her head down at you. “I know you, like, want to impress us. But really — next time, just let aurochs be. Ok?” You’ve been taking this alpha [pc.mf|bull|amazon] thing way too seriously. There will be no sexy times now — it’s enough of an effort for you to limp back to the hovercab and collapse on the backset. Still, as you convalesce while one of the twins lifts the thing into the air and begins the trip back to the spaceport, you can tell by the way they are quietly giggling and tapping at their holo-devices that you’ve certainly given them and their friends something to talk about for the next week. Hurray.

rows.original: You sharply lift your hand to the girls for them to be quiet — and then do your best to make no other sudden movements. You stand there in the shallows, water washing around your [pc.legs], and watch as the auroch laps at the water. Its giant brown eyes appear fixed on you as it does so, and you must constantly wrestle with a fight-or-flee response. Being in the presence of something this big[pc.isHeight 72| even for you,] with horns that are considerably longer than your arms, is hard to bear. A certain zen-like calm descends on you as the seconds drag by, though. The trees sigh and the water breaks gently against the rocky shore. With no sound except the huff of the giant, shaggy bovine and the surprisingly delicate drafts it takes with the navy-colored shovel that is its tongue, you are transported perhaps to a scene of what New Texas might have been like before the arrival of humans, their giant agri-machines, and their willingness to play skip-rope with their genes. It’s beautiful in a way that farm fields or even buxom cowgirls could never be. You realize you are to the auroch what a fruit-fly is to you: a passing annoyance, not worth bothering with so long as it leaves you alone. You are calm. After a couple of minutes, and with a mucus-y explosion of a snort, it turns and lumbers back from whence it came, tail lashing at the undergrowth. “Woooowwww.” A small, pale hand works its way into your own right hand. “You don’t see those too often ‘round here!” “Must’ve come down from the high steppe.” A separate small, pale hand slides into your left hand. “The bulls hunt ‘em sometimes, in winter. You gotta get a license, though. There ain’t many left.” The twins are talking in low tones, pupils dilated and giggling a little unsteadily, some of the raw majesty of the encounter having impacted on them also. You go back to the picnic and eat it in relatively quiet circumspection.
rows.translation: 你猛地朝姑娘们抬手，示意她们安静——随后尽力不再做出任何突然动作。 你站在浅水中，水流冲刷着[pc.legs]，注视原牛舔水。它喝水时，巨大的棕色眼睛似乎始终盯着你，你不得不不断压制战斗或逃跑的本能反应。面对一个如此庞大的东西[pc.isHeight 72|，即使对你而言也是如此，]实在很难承受，更何况它的长角远比你的手臂还长。 然而随着时间流逝，某种禅意般的平静降临在你身上。树木轻叹，水流温柔地拍打岩石岸边。除了巨大蓬毛牛兽的喘息，以及它用那条宛如深蓝铲子的舌头出乎意料地轻巧饮水的声音，再无其他动静。你仿佛被带到新德克萨斯在人类、巨型农业机器，以及他们拿自己的基因玩跳绳的意愿到来之前的景象。那是一种农田乃至丰满牛姑娘都永远无法企及的美。你意识到，自己之于原牛，就如同果蝇之于你：只要不来招惹，不过是一点转瞬即逝、不值得理会的烦扰。你平静下来。 几分钟后，它带着一声黏液四溅的响鼻转过身，拖着沉重身躯返回来处，尾巴抽打灌木丛。 “哇啊啊啊。”一只苍白小手探进你的右手。“这附近可不常见到它们！” “肯定是从高原上下来的。”另一只苍白小手滑进你的左手。“公牛们冬天有时会猎杀它们。不过得申请许可证。现在剩下的不多了。” 双胞胎用低沉语气交谈，瞳孔放大，笑声有些不稳，显然这次遭遇的原始壮丽也冲击了她们。你回到野餐处，在相对安静的沉思中吃起东西。

rows.original: You’re idling in the cool water, wondering what to do next, when you hear the sound of packing up coming from the beach. The twins are in the process of taking everything back to the hovercab. Wait, they want to leave? “Yep!” Carrie has her nose firmly in the air. “Sick of the swimmin’ hole now.” “Some folk don’t know how to treat it!” Cora opines. “Or cowgirls.” “And that!” But... wait a minute!... ah, damnit. You’ve little choice but to slink back to the beach, dry off and then clamber back into the driver’s seat. All attempts at lightening the mood or apologising for your behaviour are met with stony silence and ‘hmph’s. Perhaps the forlorn figure you cut by the time you land the cab back down on Big T’s ranch very slightly softens Carrie’s attitude towards you, because she squeezes your arm as she and her sister are vacating themselves from the backseat. “We can do this again, maybe,” she says. “But next time... try ‘n remember to bring your A-game and be a lil more considerate, alright [pc.mf |mister |missy ]?” You take the hovercab back to the hire place.[flags.CARRIE_SWIMMING_CATCH | Well... at least you got a fish out of it. ]

rows.original: [var0 |Humming a tune to herself, Cora wades her red swimsuit-clad form out towards the centre of the pool, until the water is almost up to her tail. “I think I might borrow [pc.name] for a lil while,” she calls to her sister. “Show [pc.him] the falls. You alright with that?” “Have fun,” Carrie responds with a cool smile. She’s loosened her bikini top and has settled herself front down in a sunbeam, sunglasses on. Maybe you’ve annoyed her? Or there’s some other sisterly arrangement going on here that you aren’t privy to. Whatever. At least by the time you brought it back to the milking barn, setting down with a wavering hum in the field outside, the two sundress-wearing, auburn cowgirls — who are waiting for you with their arms full of gear — look appreciably more enthusiastic. ]

rows.original: You usher Ciaran into the hover-car. The hellhound seems fairly placid now, which you suppose must mean he’s getting close to passing out. It doesn’t take long for your taxi to reach Ciaran’s house, and you help the towering drunk out of the car. You take a moment to survey the exterior of Ciaran’s home. It’s a one-story ranch-style house in the native architectural style. There’s a front porch, and you can see what looks like a pet door built into the front door of the house. While you’re still looking, Ciaran fumbles in his pockets for the keys before finding them. “C’mon inside a minute kiddo.” He gestures for you to follow him.
rows.translation: 你把基兰扶进悬浮车。地狱犬现在显得相当安静，你猜这大概意味着他快要昏睡过去了。出租车没过多久便抵达基兰家，你扶着这个高大的醉汉下车。你花了片刻观察基兰住宅的外观。这是一栋采用当地建筑风格的单层牧场式房屋。前面有门廊，你还看见房屋正门上似乎装着宠物门。你仍在打量时，基兰在口袋里摸索钥匙，终于把它找了出来。“进来坐一会儿吧，小家伙。”他示意你跟上。

rows.original: You had intended to see him inside anyway, so you accept the offer and enter the older man’s home. Ciaran closes the door behind you and stumbles into the nearby kitchen. He calls out from the other room “Make yourself at home, kid. I’ll just be a minute.” You meander into the living room. The interior the home seems to be mostly wood, a rich mahogany that accentuates the rustic decor. You can certainly tell this is the home of an unmarried man, but it’s not a total wreck like so many bachelor pads. While the place is definitely disheveled, there seems to be a sense of order to the mess, and everything seems very clean, even if not very tidy. There are clothes scattered across the couch, which along with all the other furniture, is sized for someone of Ciaran’s proportions. On the walls are various hunting trophies, along with a few antique firearms from various cultures and time periods
rows.translation: 你本来就打算把他送进屋，于是接受邀请，进入这个年长男人的家。基兰在你身后关门，踉跄着走进附近的厨房。他从另一个房间喊道：“当自己家吧，孩子。我马上回来。”你漫步进入客厅。房屋内部似乎大多由木材构成，浓郁的桃花心木色更衬托出质朴装潢。你当然能看出这是一个未婚男人的家，但并不像许多单身汉住处那样彻底混乱。这里确实凌乱，却乱得颇有秩序；所有东西也都很干净，只是不够整齐。沙发上散落着衣服，而沙发和所有其他家具一样，尺寸都适合基兰这样的体型。墙上挂着各种狩猎战利品，还有几件来自不同文化与时代的古董枪械

rows.original: and several photographs. Almost all of the pictures are of a girl with lavender hair and fur, two fluffy tails, and golden eyes: she’s an ausar/kaithrit hybrid. There are pictures of her at several different ages being held by or posing with a smiling ausar man with black hair and fur streaked with white. Every photograph depicts the girl winning some sort of academic or athletic award, and the man looking very proud of her. When you see the most recent photo, you realize the man is Ciaran before taking the Treatment. He apparently had no horns and was much shorter and less muscular, though still powerfully-built for an ausar, and with the same tattered ear. Could that mean the girl with him is his daughter?
rows.translation: 还有几张照片。几乎所有照片里都是同一个有薰衣草色头发与毛发、两条蓬松尾巴和金色眼睛的女孩：她是奥萨尔与凯斯利特的混血。照片中不同年龄的她被一个黑色头发与毛发中夹杂白丝、面带笑容的奥萨尔男人抱着，或与他合影。每一张照片都记录了女孩赢得某种学术或体育奖项的时刻，男人则显得无比为她自豪。看到最新照片时，你意识到那个男人是接受改造疗程前的基兰。他那时显然没有角，身材也矮小、没那么健壮，尽管以奥萨尔标准而言依旧强壮有力，耳朵也同样残破。难道这意味着照片里的女孩是他的女儿？

rows.original: Before you can ponder it further you hear Ciaran walking into the room. When you turn to face him you notice he’s bare from the waist up. His sculpted torso is covered in a multitude of scars of various sizes, shapes, and origins. He flops his hand at you lazily as he pulls off his belt and mutters, “Stand down, marine. I’m going to sleep.” Ciaran kicks off his boots before he topples face-first onto the couch, passing out almost immediately. You stand there awkwardly for a moment before shrugging to yourself. It doesn’t seem the most comfortable place to sleep, but you suppose he at least won’t choke in his sleep.
rows.translation: 你还没来得及深思，就听见基兰走进房间。转身面对他时，你发现他上半身赤裸。雕塑般的躯干上遍布大小、形状和来源各异的伤疤。他懒洋洋地冲你摆手，脱下腰带，嘟囔道：“解除戒备，陆战队员。我要睡觉了。”基兰踢掉靴子，随后脸朝下倒在沙发上，几乎立刻就睡着了。你尴尬地站了片刻，随后耸耸肩。这里看起来不是最舒服的睡觉地方，但至少他应该不会在睡梦中窒息。

You walk back into the saloon, ready to resume your journey.

rows.translation: 基兰装出受伤的表情：“怎么，男人就不能只和美女聊天，而不设法让她们张开腿吗？”看到你怀疑的目光，他继续说：“听着，我喜欢听女人和我说话，也喜欢和她们进行有头脑的交谈。可想和母牛好好聊一场，只能趁两次做爱之间。”他露出略带感伤的表情。“很多人把改造过的姑娘当成没脑子的迷糊蛋，所以大多数母牛没多少机会和同住男人之外的公牛聊天。可事实上，不少母牛喜欢听男性如何看待她们的想法。而且同样有很多姑娘再次发情后，喜欢用一次精彩口交回报那些圆滑、粗犷又英俊的聊天伙伴，这当然也不坏。见鬼，就算她们是妓女，通常也不会收费。她们总是说‘哦，基兰，谢谢你听我讲这些傻乎乎的小烦恼’，然后钻到桌子底下，或者坐进我怀里。我想不到还有什么比美妙的吮吸或猛烈的性交更适合结束一场愉快闲聊。”
rows.raw: "\n\nCiaran feigns a wounded expression, “What, can’t a man just talk to beautiful women without trying to get them to spread their legs?” At the dubious look you shoot him he continues, “Look, I enjoy hearing women talk to me. I also enjoy intelligent conversation with them. The only time you can get a decent chat with a cow is in between fucks.” He adopts a slightly wistful expression. “Lots of people write off Treated girls as airheaded and ditzy, so most cows don’t get to have too many chats with bulls they don’t live with. The thing is, plenty of those cows enjoy hearing a male perspective on their ideas. It also doesn’t hurt that lots of those same girls love to repay their suave, rugged, and handsome conversation partners with a good blowjob once they start getting horny again. And hell, even if they’re prostitutes they usually won’t even charge for it. It’s always ‘Oh Ciaran, let me show you my thanks for listening to my silly little problems’ before they crawl under the table or into my lap. I don’t know that there’s a better way to finish a pleasant little chat than a good suck or a hard fuck.” "

rows.original: He gives you a meaningful stare after that last sentence, his arms spread in a welcoming gesture as his pheromones practically pour off of him.
rows.translation: 说完最后一句，他意味深长地盯着你，双臂展开做出欢迎姿势，信息素几乎从身上倾泻而出。
rows.raw: "He gives you a meaningful stare after that last sentence, his arms spread in a welcoming gesture as his pheromones practically pour off of him."

rows.translation: 他翻了个白眼，却仍在微笑。“好吧，在我把你按到桌上之前，你还想问什么？”

rows.translation: 他飞快地打量你一眼，随后摇头苦笑。“不过我觉得，我们现在还是继续这场愉快闲聊比较好。”他眨眨眼，略带歉意地冲你微笑。
rows.raw: "\n\nHe eyes you for a very brief moment before shaking his head and smiling ruefully. “I think I’d rather we continue our pleasant little chat for now though.” He winks and smiles at you somewhat apologetically."

rows.original: Well, at least he let you down easy.
rows.translation: 好吧，至少他拒绝得很委婉。

rows.original: You ask him about his outfit. Why would he wear it if he doesn’t like tourists asking him about it?
rows.translation: 你问起他的服装。既然不喜欢游客因此盘问他，为什么还要穿成这样？
rows.raw: "You ask him about his outfit. Why would he wear it if he doesn’t like tourists asking him about it?"

rows.original: Ciaran sighs and lets his ears droop a bit before he answers you. “Well, I spend so much time in the saloon that the owner offered me a deal a few years back. She figured that since I was pretty much a fixture of the place, I might as well look the part. As long as I wear this ridiculous getup while I’m in here, I get free drinks. It was pretty great at first, but at this point some of the locals have made a game out of trying to get gullible tourists to believe I’m actually some sort of bandit. I enjoyed it the first year or two, because I’d garner more off-world girls paying attention to me, and I’d get to talk to them or even, hah, give them a little something to remember me by.” He pantomimes placing his hands on a set of hips and makes a few vulgar thrusts with his pelvis before laughing loudly. “The last year or so though I’ve practically become a tourist attraction, and I can hardly stand it.” His expression turns sour. “You would not believe how hard it is to get some rich asshole from the core to stop asking you questions without resorting to putting your fist through his face. Thankfully Kithran and her girls are always there before I can lose my temper.”
rows.translation: 基兰叹了口气，耳朵微微垂下，随后回答：“嗯，我在酒馆里待的时间太长，几年前老板娘就和我谈了笔交易。她觉得既然我几乎成了这里的固定摆设，至少也该看起来像那么回事。只要我在这里穿着这套可笑行头，就能免费喝酒。起初确实很棒，可到了现在，有些本地人甚至把哄骗轻信游客相信我真是某种强盗当成游戏。头一两年我还挺享受，因为会有更多外世界姑娘注意我，我可以和她们聊天，甚至，哈，给她们留下一点关于我的纪念。”他假装把双手搭在一对臀部上，骨盆做了几下粗俗的挺动，随后放声大笑。“可过去一年左右，我几乎成了旅游景点，实在受不了。”他表情转为厌恶。“你根本想不到，要让某个来自核心星域的有钱混蛋停止盘问，又不一拳打穿他的脸有多难。幸好基斯兰和她的姑娘们总能在我发火之前赶到。”
rows.raw: "\n\nCiaran sighs and lets his ears droop a bit before he answers you. “Well, I spend so much time in the saloon that the owner offered me a deal a few years back. She figured that since I was pretty much a fixture of the place, I might as well look the part. As long as I wear this ridiculous getup while I’m in here, I get free drinks. It was pretty great at first, but at this point some of the locals have made a game out of trying to get gullible tourists to believe I’m actually some sort of bandit. I enjoyed it the first year or two, because I’d garner more off-world girls paying attention to me, and I’d get to talk to them or even, hah, give them a little something to remember me by.” He pantomimes placing his hands on a set of hips and makes a few vulgar thrusts with his pelvis before laughing loudly. “The last year or so though I’ve practically become a tourist attraction, and I can hardly stand it.” His expression turns sour. “You would not believe how hard it is to get some rich asshole from the core to stop asking you questions without resorting to putting your fist through his face. Thankfully Kithran and her girls are always there before I can lose my temper.”"

rows.original: You aren’t too surprised to hear that. From what you’ve gathered in your time spent with her, Ms. Kittie seems like she’d be quite skilled at making peace. Between her physique, her Treated instinct to ensure cooperation, and her skill at controlling others, you imagine the Bucking Bronco doesn’t see too many fights. When you look back at Ciaran after considering this however, you notice that he’s gazing out the window at Ms. Kittie with a blush and an almost bashful look on his face!
rows.translation: 你听到这些并不太惊讶。根据与基蒂女士相处时了解到的情况，她似乎很擅长维持和平。凭她的体格、改造者确保合作的本能，以及控制他人的技巧，你猜跃马酒馆不会发生太多打斗。然而你思考过后再看向基兰，却发现他正隔着窗户望向基蒂女士，脸上泛红，神情几乎有些腼腆！
rows.raw: "\n\nYou aren’t too surprised to hear that. From what you’ve gathered in your time spent with her, Ms. Kittie seems like she’d be quite skilled at making peace. Between her physique, her Treated instinct to ensure cooperation, and her skill at controlling others, you imagine the Bucking Bronco doesn’t see too many fights. When you look back at Ciaran after considering this however, you notice that he’s gazing out the window at Ms. Kittie with a blush and an almost bashful look on his face!"

rows.original: The hellhound must have quite a history with the imposing kaithrit madam if she can turn a predator like him bashful!
rows.translation: 如果她能让基兰这样的掠食者害羞，这只地狱犬和威严的凯斯利特鸨母之间肯定有不少往事！
rows.raw: "\n\nThe hellhound must have quite a history with the imposing kaithrit madam if she can turn a predator like him bashful!"

rows.original: You raise an eyebrow at him, not sure of who he means.
rows.translation: 你挑起一边眉毛，不确定他说的是谁。
rows.raw: "\n\nYou raise an eyebrow at him, not sure of who he means."

rows.original: Your hellhound companion’s smile returns. “You didn’t meet her on the way in? Kithran, or as she calls herself on the clock ‘Ms. Kittie.’ She’s the madam of the Broodmare Bordello, the brothel upstairs.” He jabs his thick, furred thumb upwards twice. “The locals just call it the Cathouse though since almost half the girls who work for her are her daughters. That woman’s been in this business since before the Bucking Bronco opened. I’m probably her best john. Kithran, well...” Ciaran pauses, seemingly at a loss for words. You’re shocked to see he’s actually blushing! When he finds the right words, they all seem to spill out at once. “She reminds me of old times, in the best way. I’ll leave it at that.” The normally cocksure ausar suddenly pulls his hat brim down to cover his cheeks, hiding his blush from you!
rows.translation: 地狱犬同伴重新露出笑容。“你进来时没见过她？基斯兰，或者她上班时自称的‘基蒂女士’。她是楼上妓院——种马妓院的鸨母。”他用粗壮多毛的拇指向上戳了两下。“不过本地人只叫那里猫屋，因为替她工作的姑娘近一半都是她女儿。那个女人在跃马酒馆开门前就做这行了。我大概是她最好的嫖客。基斯兰，嗯...”基兰停顿下来，似乎找不到合适的词。你震惊地发现，他居然真的脸红了！等找到合适的话，所有词语顿时倾泻而出。“她会让我想起过去的时光，而且是以最美好的方式。就说到这里吧。”平时自信满满的奥萨尔突然把帽檐拉下来遮住脸颊，不让你看见他的羞红！
rows.raw: "\n\nYour hellhound companion’s smile returns. “You didn’t meet her on the way in? Kithran, or as she calls herself on the clock ‘Ms. Kittie.’ She’s the madam of the Broodmare Bordello, the brothel upstairs.” He jabs his thick, furred thumb upwards twice. “The locals just call it the Cathouse though since almost half the girls who work for her are her daughters. That woman’s been in this business since before the Bucking Bronco opened. I’m probably her best john. Kithran, well...” Ciaran pauses, seemingly at a loss for words. I’ll leave it at that.” The normally cocksure ausar suddenly pulls his hat brim down to cover his cheeks, hiding his blush from you!"

rows.translation: 你和基兰的交谈暂时陷入沉默时，他露出傻乎乎的笑容，斜眼看向你，打破安静。“喜欢笑话吗，孩子？”
rows.raw: "During a lull in your conversation with Ciaran, he cracks a goofy smile and gives you a sidelong stare before breaking the silence. “Do you like jokes, kid?”"

rows.translation: 你热情地点头，问基兰知不知道什么好笑话。
rows.raw: "\n\nYou nod your head enthusiastically and ask Ciaran if he knows any good ones. "

rows.original: You shrug your shoulders and tell Ciaran it depends on if the joke is any good or not.
rows.translation: 你耸耸肩，告诉基兰这得看笑话到底好不好笑。
